daily_reality.typical_workday: Eight-hour days, five days per week, primarily at microscope. Screen Pap smears and other specimens for abnormal cells. Process gynecological cases (cervical cancer screening), non-gynecological cases (body fluids, respiratory, urinary specimens), and fine needle aspirations (tumor diagnosis). Collaborate with pathologists on findings. Document results, perform quality control checks. CLIA-regulated workload limits apply.
daily_reality.deadlines: Turnaround times for cytology results (Pap smears typically 1-2 weeks). Proficiency testing deadlines. ASCP certification renewal every 3 years. CLIA compliance deadlines. CAP accreditation cycles.
daily_reality.seasonality: Relatively consistent year-round workload. Cervical cancer screening campaigns may create periodic volume increases. Academic lab work follows semester cycles.

laws_and_standards: CLIA workload limits (max 100 slides per 24 hours)
regulatory.licensing: CT(ASCP) certification from American Society for Clinical Pathology required. Bachelor's degree in cytotechnology or related field. Completion of accredited cytotechnology program. $250 exam fee, 100 multiple-choice questions. Renewal every 3 years with continuing education. Transitioning to Master's degree requirement (some programs starting Fall 2026). Some states require additional state licensure.
regulatory.penalties: CLIA sanctions: fines, suspension, or revocation of lab certificate. Loss of ASCP certification for CE non-compliance. CAP accreditation loss. New CMS guidance (Sept 2025) discontinuing remote digital slide review discretion — labs must have separate CLIA certificates by March 2026.

career_psychology.motivation: Critical role in cancer detection (cervical, lung, thyroid); detective-like work identifying abnormal cells; direct impact on patient outcomes; specialized expertise valued in healthcare.
career_psychology.burnout: Repetitive microscopy causing eye strain and physical fatigue; staffing shortages forcing overtime and double shifts; high-stakes work (missed cancer diagnosis); CLIA workload caps help but understaffing creates pressure. Profession exploring career advancement opportunities and technology integration to mitigate burnout.

market.job_count_estimate: Small niche within ~340,000 medical laboratory technologists. ~500 unfilled positions nationally. 16% expected to retire within 5 years. Concentrated in hospitals, reference labs, and academic medical centers.
market.work_arrangements: Primarily laboratory-based on-site work. Standard daytime shifts. Some reference labs offer evening/weekend coverage. Remote digital slide review being limited by new CMS guidance (March 2026 deadline for separate CLIA certificates). Profession transitioning from bachelor's to master's degree requirement.
